cohort: 80 female patients undergoing cesarean section were randomized into two groups to receive either hyperbaric bupivacaine or levobupivacaine.
finding: Levobupivacaine was associated with a significantly lower incidence of hypotension (45% vs. 62.5%) compared to hyperbaric bupivacaine, while other outcomes like onset, duration of anesthesia, patient satisfaction, and neonatal outcomes were comparable.
